'''津守'''（つもり）氏は、[[住吉大社]]（[[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[住吉区]]）の歴代宮司の一族で、古代以来の連綿とした系譜を持つ名族。 == 出自 == 津守氏は、[[尾張氏]]の一族で[[摂津国]][[住吉郡]]の豪族の[[田蓑宿禰]]の子孫。
田蓑宿禰が「七道の浜」（[[大阪府]][[堺市]]七道）で[[三韓征伐|新羅征伐]]から帰還した[[神功皇后]]を迎えた時、神功皇后が[[住吉三神]]の神功があったことから、田蓑宿禰に住吉三神を祀るように言い、田蓑宿禰の子の豊吾団に津守の姓を与えたのが始まり。 == 遣唐使神主 == == 南朝方御座所 ==

[[津守大海]]
[[津守吉祥]]
[[津守国夏]]
[[津守国基]]
[[津守国美]]
[[津守国栄]] |後裔 = [[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]） }} '''津守氏'''（つもりうじ）は、「津守」を[[氏]]の名とする[[氏族]]。 [[住吉大社]]（[[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[住吉区]]）の歴代宮司の一族で、古代以来の系譜を持つ氏族である。 __TOC__ {{clear}} == 出自 == 津守氏は、[[綿津見神|綿積豊玉彦命]]または[[天火明命]]の流れをくむ一族であり、[[摂津国]][[住吉郡]]の[[豪族]]の[[田蓑宿禰]]の子孫である。田蓑宿禰が「七道の浜」（[[大阪府]][[堺市]]七道）（当時は住吉郡）において[[200年]]に[[三韓征伐|新羅征伐]]から帰還した[[神功皇后]]を迎えた時、[[神功皇后]]が[[住吉三神]]の神功があったことから、田蓑宿禰に住吉三神を{{読み仮名|祀|まつ}}るように言い、田蓑宿禰の子の[[豊吾田連]]（とよあたのむらじ）と屋主足尼（やぬしのすくね）に'''津守連'''の[[カバネ|姓]]を与えたのが始まり。豊吾田連の8世孫である津守広麿（[[津守吉祥]]の子）が[[天武天皇]]十三年に'''津守宿禰'''に改姓された[[宝賀寿男]]「第3章 地祇系氏族　第2節 海神族（2）尾張氏族　10尾張連（一）、尾張宿祢（一）」『古代氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1294頁。宝賀寿男「第3章 地祇系氏族　第2節 海神族（2）尾張氏族　10津守連（一）、津守宿祢」『古代氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、1986年、1330頁。。津守とは「津（港）」を「守る」という意味で、港の管理を職掌とした。 == 遣唐使神主 == * [[住吉津]] == 南朝御座所 == * [[住吉行宮]] == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 関連項目 == * [[大海神社]] * [[津守寺]] * [[新後撰和歌集]] {{DEFAULTSORT:つもりし}} [[Category:津守氏|*]] [[Category:氏]] [[category:日本の氏族]] [[Category:近畿地方の氏族]] [[Category:住吉大社]] [[Category:住吉郡]] [[Category:住吉区の歴史]]

[[津守国栄]] |後裔 = [[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]） }} '''津守氏'''（つもりうじ）は、「津守」を[[氏]]の名とする[[氏族]]。 [[住吉大社]]（[[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[住吉区]]）の歴代宮司の一族で、古代以来の系譜を持つ氏族である。 __TOC__ {{clear}} == 出自 == 津守氏は、[[天火明命]]の流れをくむ一族であり、[[摂津国]][[住吉郡]]の[[豪族]]の[[田蓑宿禰]]の子孫である。田蓑宿禰が「七道の浜」（[[大阪府]][[堺市]]七道）（当時は住吉郡）において[[200年]]に[[三韓征伐|新羅征伐]]から帰還した[[神功皇后]]を迎えた時、[[神功皇后]]が[[住吉三神]]の神功があったことから、田蓑宿禰に住吉三神を{{読み仮名|祀|まつ}}るように言われている。津守とは「津（港）」を「守る」という意味で、港の管理を職掌とした。 なお、『[[住吉大社神代記]]』によれば、[[垂仁天皇]]と[[景行天皇]]の頃には、意弥那宜多命（おみながたのみこと）の子の意富弥多足尼（おおみたのすくね）が活動していたという田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年）。 == 遣唐使神主 == * [[住吉津]] == 南朝御座所 == * [[住吉行宮]] == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 関連項目 == * [[大海神社]] * [[津守寺]] * [[新後撰和歌集]] {{DEFAULTSORT:つもりし}} [[Category:津守氏|*]] [[Category:氏]] [[category:日本の氏族]] [[Category:近畿地方の氏族]] [[Category:住吉大社]] [[Category:住吉郡]] [[Category:住吉区の歴史]]

[[津守国栄]] |後裔 = [[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]） }} '''津守氏'''（つもりうじ）は、[[社家]]・[[華族]]だった[[日本]]の[[氏族]]。古代以来の系譜を持ち、[[住吉大社]]（[[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[住吉区]]）の宮司を世襲した一族で、[[明治維新|維新]]後には華族の[[男爵]]家にも列した{{sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|p=650}}。 __TOC__ {{clear}} == 歴史 == 津守氏は、[[天火明命]]の流れをくむ一族とされる{{sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|p=650}}。『[[住吉大社神代記]]』によれば、[[垂仁天皇]]と[[景行天皇]]の頃には、意弥那宜多命（おみながたのみこと）の子の意富弥多足尼（おおみたのすくね）が活動していたという田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年）。 [[摂津国]][[住吉郡]]の[[豪族]]田蓑宿禰を祖とすると伝えられる{{Kotobank|1=津守氏|2=日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}}。田蓑宿禰が「七道の浜」（[[大阪府]][[堺市]]七道）（当時は住吉郡）において[[200年]]に[[三韓征伐|新羅征伐]]から帰還した[[神功皇后]]を迎えた時、[[神功皇后]]が[[住吉三神]]の神功があったことから、田蓑宿禰に住吉三神を{{読み仮名|祀|まつ}}るように言われている。 [[大和平野]]への入口である[[淀川]]河口付近は早くから交通の要衝として栄え、津守氏は津（港）を守護する職務を大和朝廷より与えられており、津守の氏族名もそれに由来している。住吉神社に奉仕しつつ、海部を率いて航海術を掌握。津守氏を称したことが確認できるのは[[津守宿禰国磨]]の代からであり、彼は[[遣唐使]]の一員として渡海した。 住吉系図・住吉神主并一族系図によれば、11世紀後半の[[津守国基|国基]]は、津守氏中興の祖と呼ばれているという。[[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]の[[津守国夏|国夏]]と[[津守国久|国久]]は、南朝の将として活躍した。 [[津守国美|国美]]の代の明治4年（1871年）に名門社家として[[華族]]に列せられ、明治17年（1884年）7月8日に[[男爵]]に列せられた{{sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|p=650}}{{sfn|小田部雄次|2006|p=33/340}}。 == 遣唐使神主 == * [[住吉津]] == 南朝御座所 == * [[住吉行宮]] == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * {{Cite book|和書|date=1994年（平成6年）|title=華族誕生 名誉と体面の明治|author=浅見雅男|authorlink=浅見雅男|publisher=[[リブロポート]]|ref=harv}} * {{Cite book|和書|date=1990年（平成2年）|title=華族大鑑|series=日本人物誌叢書7|author=華族大鑑刊行会|publisher=[[日本図書センター]]|isbn=978-4820540342|ref=harv}} == 関連項目 == * [[大海神社]] * [[津守寺]] * [[新後撰和歌集]] {{リダイレクトの所属カテゴリ |redirect1=津守家 |1-1= 社家 |1-2= 日本の男爵家 }} {{DEFAULTSORT:つもりし}} [[Category:津守氏|*]] [[Category:氏]] [[category:日本の氏族]] [[Category:近畿地方の氏族]] [[Category:住吉大社]] [[Category:住吉郡]] [[Category:住吉区の歴史]]

revision.text:
The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}}</ref> They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''<ref name=":02">{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}</ref>. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of [[Sumiyoshi-taisha|Sumiyoshi taisha]] since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan).
In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|ja|天道根命|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine}}, together with the descendants of Amenohoakari are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from [[Takamagahara]] (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en}} clans.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}}</ref>
However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of Amenohoakari, is a forged document,<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kokuho「Amabe-shi Keizu」he no gimon, Kokigi no Heya (国宝「海部氏系図」への疑問 古樹紀之房間)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}}</ref> and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original [[genealogy]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}}</ref>
== References == {{Reflist}}{{Draft categories|[[:Category:Japanese clans]] [[:Category:Owari clan]] Wikipedia drafts[[:Category:Shake clans]] [[:Category:Draft articles]] [[:Category:Kuni no miyatsuko families]] }}

[[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}}'''The Tsumori clan''' was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was a shrine family and aristocrat . The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} Shrine ( [[:ja:住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward,]] [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en}} (literally, the Central Land of Reed Plains) in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi [[:ja:住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki]], during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, [[:ja:豪族|a powerful]] lord in [[:ja:住吉郡|Sumiyoshi County, Settsu]] [[Settsu Province|Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from [[:ja:三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla]] in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress]] Jingu had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the [[:ja:淀川|Yodo]] River, which is the entrance to [[:ja:奈良盆地|the Yamato Plain]], flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of [[津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa]], who traveled to the sea as a member of [[:ja:遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions]] . [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}}'''The Tsumori clan''' was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was a shrine family and aristocrat . The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} Shrine ( [[:ja:住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward,]] [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en}} (literally, the Central Land of Reed Plains) in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi [[:ja:住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki]], during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, [[:ja:豪族|a powerful]] lord in [[:ja:住吉郡|Sumiyoshi County, Settsu]] [[Settsu Province|Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from [[:ja:三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla]] in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress]] Jingu had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the [[:ja:淀川|Yodo]] River, which is the entrance to [[:ja:奈良盆地|the Yamato Plain]], flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of [[津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa]], who traveled to the sea as a member of [[:ja:遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions]] . [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}}'''The Tsumori clan''' was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was a shrine family and aristocrat . The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en}} (literally, the Central Land of Reed Plains) in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|a powerful}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi County, Settsu}} [[Settsu Province|Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress]] Jingu had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo}} River, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|the Yamato Plain}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions}} . [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}}'''The Tsumori clan''' was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was a shrine family and aristocrat . The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en}} (literally, the Central Land of Reed Plains) in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|a powerful}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi County, Settsu}} [[Settsu Province|Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress]] Jingu had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo}} River, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|the Yamato Plain}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions}} . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]], {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even ranked as {{ill|10=ja|11=公卿|Kugyō|lt=nobles}} . {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} In 1871, during {{ill|10=ja|11=津守國榮|Kunimi}} 's reign, he was elevated to the peerage as a member of a prestigious shrine family, and on July 8, 1884, he was elevated to the rank of [[baron]] . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|小田部雄次|2006}} == Priest of the Japanese envoy to the Tang Dynasty == * {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉津|Sumiyoshi Port}} == Southern Court Throne Room == * {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉行宮|Sumiyoshi Imperial Palace}} [[en:draft:Tsumori clan]] [[ja:津守氏]] == footnote == {{脚注ヘルプ}}{{Reflist}} == References == * {{Cite book|title=華族誕生 名誉と体面の明治|last=浅見雅男|date=1994年（平成6年）|publisher=[[リブロポート]]|ref=harv|author-link=浅見雅男|和書}} * {{Cite book|title=華族大鑑|last=華族大鑑刊行会|date=1990年（平成2年）|publisher=[[日本図書センター]]|isbn=978-4820540342|series=日本人物誌叢書7|ref=harv|和書}}{{Cite book|title=華族大鑑|last=華族大鑑刊行会|date=1990年（平成2年）|publisher=[[日本図書センター]]|isbn=978-4820540342|series=日本人物誌叢書7|ref=harv|和書}} * {{Cite book|title=日本名門・名家大辞典|last=森岡浩|date=2012年（平成24年）|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=978-4-490-10821-7|ref=harv|author-link=森岡浩|和書}}{{Cite book|title=日本名門・名家大辞典|last=森岡浩|date=2012年（平成24年）|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=978-4-490-10821-7|ref=harv|author-link=森岡浩|和書}} == Related item == * [[新後撰和歌集|Oumi Shrine]] * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} * [[新後撰和歌集|New Collection of Waka Poets]] {{Authority control}}

[[津守国栄]] |後裔 = [[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]） }} '''津守氏'''（つもりうじ）は、[[社家]]・[[華族]]だった[[日本]]の[[氏族]]。古代以来の系譜を持ち、[[住吉大社]]（[[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[住吉区]]）の宮司を世襲した一族で、[[明治維新|維新]]後には華族の[[男爵]]家にも列した{{sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|p=650}}。 __TOC__ {{clear}} == 歴史 == 津守氏は、[[天火明命]]の流れをくむ一族と伝えられる{{sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|p=650}}{{sfn|森岡浩|2012|p=324}}。『[[住吉大社神代記]]』によれば、[[垂仁天皇]]と[[景行天皇]]の頃には、意弥那宜多命（おみながたのみこと）の子の意富弥多足尼（おおみたのすくね）が活動していたという田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年）。 [[摂津国]][[住吉郡]]の[[豪族]]田蓑宿禰を祖とすると伝えられる{{Kotobank|1=津守氏|2=日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}}。田蓑宿禰が「七道の浜」（[[大阪府]][[堺市]]七道）（当時は住吉郡）において[[200年]]に[[三韓征伐|新羅征伐]]から帰還した[[神功皇后]]を迎えた時、[[神功皇后]]が[[住吉三神]]の神功があったことから、田蓑宿禰に住吉三神を{{読み仮名|祀|まつ}}るように言われている。 また[[大和平野]]への入口である[[淀川]]河口付近は早くから交通の要衝として栄えていたため、津（港）を守護する職務を大和朝廷より与えられており、津守の氏族名もそれに由来している。代々住吉神社に奉仕しつつ、海部を率いて航海術を掌握。津守氏を称したことが確認できるのは[[津守宿禰国磨]]の代からであり、彼は[[遣唐使]]の一員として渡海した。 平安後期の[[津守国基|国基]]は歌人としても著名であるなど神官として以外も活躍{{sfn|森岡浩|2012|p=324}}。住吉系図・住吉神主并一族系図によれば、国基は、津守氏中興の祖と呼ばれているという。[[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]の[[津守国夏|国夏]]と[[津守国久|国久]]は、南朝の武将として活躍した{{sfn|森岡浩|2012|p=324}}。江戸時代には[[公卿]]に列する者もあった{{sfn|森岡浩|2012|p=324}}。 [[津守国美|国美]]の代の明治4年（1871年）に名門社家として[[華族]]に列せられ、明治17年（1884年）7月8日に[[男爵]]に列せられた{{sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|p=650}}{{sfn|小田部雄次|2006|p=33/340}}。 == 遣唐使神主 == * [[住吉津]] == 南朝御座所 == * [[住吉行宮]] == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * {{Cite book|和書|date=1994年（平成6年）|title=華族誕生 名誉と体面の明治|author=浅見雅男|authorlink=浅見雅男|publisher=[[リブロポート]]|ref=harv}} * {{Cite book|和書|date=1990年（平成2年）|title=華族大鑑|series=日本人物誌叢書7|author=華族大鑑刊行会|publisher=[[日本図書センター]]|isbn=978-4820540342|ref=harv}} * {{Cite book|和書|date=2012年（平成24年）|title=日本名門・名家大辞典 |author= 森岡浩|authorlink= 森岡浩|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn= 978-4-490-10821-7|ref=harv}} == 関連項目 == * [[大海神社]] * [[津守寺]] * [[新後撰和歌集]] {{Normdaten}} {{リダイレクトの所属カテゴリ |redirect1=津守家 |1-1= 社家 |1-2= 日本の男爵家 }} {{DEFAULTSORT:つもりうし}} [[Category:津守氏|!]] [[Category:氏]] [[category:日本の氏族]] [[Category:近畿地方の氏族]] [[Category:住吉大社|氏つもりうし]] [[Category:住吉郡]] [[Category:住吉区の歴史]]

[[津守国夏]]

[[津守国美]]
[[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}}{{complex}} '''The Tsumori clan''' was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic {{ill|Shrine family|en|Shake_(social_class)|10=ja|11=社家}}. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en||fr}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed}}''}} in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|Gōzoku|lt=a powerful}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo River}}, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|Nara Basin|lt=the Yamato Plain}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions}} . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}}{{complex}} '''The Tsumori clan''' was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic {{ill|Shrine family|en|Shake_(social_class)|10=ja|11=社家}}. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en||fr}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed}}''}} in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|Gōzoku|lt=a powerful}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo River}}, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|Nara Basin|lt=the Yamato Plain}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions}} . and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}}{{complex}} '''The Tsumori clan''' was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic {{ill|Shrine family|en|Shake_(social_class)|10=ja|11=社家}}. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en||fr}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed}}''}} in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|Gōzoku|lt=a powerful}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo River}}, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|Nara Basin|lt=the Yamato Plain}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions}} . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]], {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even ranked as {{ill|10=ja|11=公卿|Kugyō|lt=nobles}} . {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} In 1871, during {{ill|10=ja|11=津守國榮|Kunimi}} 's reign, he was elevated to the peerage as a member of a prestigious shrine family, and on July 8, 1884, he was elevated to the rank of [[baron]] . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|小田部雄次|2006}} == Genealogy == {| class="wikitable" ! colspan="7" |Source{{Cite They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en||fr}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed}}''}} in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|Gōzoku|lt=a powerful}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo River}}, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|Nara Basin|lt=the Yamato Plain}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions}} . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]], {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even ranked as {{ill|10=ja|11=公卿|Kugyō|lt=nobles}} . {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} In 1871, during {{ill|10=ja|11=津守國榮|Kunimi}} 's reign, he was elevated to the peerage as a member of a prestigious shrine family, and on July 8, 1884, he was elevated to the rank of [[baron]] . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|小田部雄次|2006}} == Genealogy == {| class="wikitable" ! colspan="7" |Source{{Cite In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998年） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|Gōzoku|lt=a powerful}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo River}}, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|Nara Basin|lt=the Yamato Plain}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions}} . and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}}{{complex}} '''The Tsumori clan''' was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic {{ill|lt=Shrine family|Shake (social class)|en|Shake_(social_class)|10=ja|11=社家}}. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{Ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en||fr}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed}}''}} in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en}}, {{ill|Ame-no-hohi|en}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr||ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft||simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族).
