[[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}} '''The Tsumori clan''' (津守氏) was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic {{ill|lt=Shrine family|Shake (social class)|en|Shake_(social_class)|10=ja|11=社家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/lt=Shrine family|qq=}}. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net|qq=draft|qq=draft}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato kingship|qq=}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayato people|qq=}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|qq=}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amabe clan|qq=}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takakuraji|qq=}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998th year ） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|Gōzoku|lt=a powerful|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo River|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|Nara Basin|lt=the Yamato Plain|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]], {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even Ranked as {{ill|10=ja|11=Kugyō|Kugyō|lt=nobles|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} . {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} In 1871, during {{ill|10=ja|11=津守國榮|Kunimi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} 's reign, he was elevated to the peerage as a member of a prestigious shrine family, and on July 8, 1884, he was elevated to the Rank of [[baron]] . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|小田部雄次|2006}} == Genealogy == {| class="wikitable" ! colspan="7" |Source{{Cite [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}} '''The Tsumori clan''' (津守氏) was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic {{ill|lt=Shrine family|Shake (social class)|en|Shake_(social_class)|10=ja|11=社家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/lt=Shrine family|qq=}}. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net|qq=draft|qq=draft}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato kingship|qq=}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayato people|qq=}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|qq=}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amabe clan|qq=}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takakuraji|qq=}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998th year ） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|Gōzoku|lt=a powerful|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo River|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|Nara Basin|lt=the Yamato Plain|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even Ranked as [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}} '''The Tsumori clan''' (津守氏) was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic {{ill|lt=Shrine family|Shake (social class)|en|Shake_(social_class)|10=ja|11=社家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/lt=Shrine family|qq=}}. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} Shrine ( {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉区|Sumiyoshi Ward|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net|qq=draft|qq=draft}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato kingship|qq=}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayato people|qq=}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|qq=}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|lt=Amabe|ja|海部氏|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amabe clan|qq=}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takakuraji|qq=}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998th year ） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, {{ill|10=ja|11=豪族|Gōzoku|lt=a powerful|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the {{ill|10=ja|11=淀川|Yodo River|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which is the entrance to {{ill|10=ja|11=奈良盆地|Nara Basin|lt=the Yamato Plain|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of {{ill|10=ja|11=遣唐使|the Tang Dynasty missions|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} were active as [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}} '''The Tsumori clan''' (津守氏) was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic [[:en:Shake (social class)|Shrine family]]. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} Shrine ( [[:en:Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Sumiyoshi Ward]], [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net|qq=draft|qq=draft}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato kingship|qq=}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayato people|qq=}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|qq=}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Amabe clan|Amabe]], and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, [[:en:Takakuraji|Takakuraji]], as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998th year ） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, [[:en:Gōzoku|a powerful]] lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the [[:en:Yodo River|Yodo River]], which is the entrance to [[:en:Nara Basin|the Yamato Plain]], flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of [[:en:Japanese missions to Tang China|the Tang Dynasty missions]] . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]], {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even Ranked as {{ill|10=ja|11=Kugyō|Kugyō|lt=nobles|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} . {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} In 1871, during {{ill|10=ja|11=津守國榮|Kunimi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} 's reign, he was elevated to the peerage as a member of a prestigious shrine family, and on July 8, 1884, he was elevated to the Rank of [[baron]] . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|小田部雄次|2006}} == Genealogy == {| class="wikitable" ! colspan="7" |Source{{Cite [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}} '''The Tsumori clan''' (津守氏) was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic [[:en:Shake (social class)|Shrine family]]. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} Shrine ( [[:en:Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Sumiyoshi Ward]], [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net|qq=draft|qq=draft}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato kingship|qq=}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayato people|qq=}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|qq=}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Amabe clan|Amabe]], and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, [[:en:Takakuraji|Takakuraji]], as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998th year ） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, [[:en:Gōzoku|a powerful]] lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the [[:en:Yodo River|Yodo River]], which is the entrance to [[:en:Nara Basin|the Yamato Plain]], flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of [[:en:Japanese missions to Tang China|the Tang Dynasty missions]] . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]], {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even Ranked as {{ill|10=ja|11=Kugyō|Kugyō|lt=nobles|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} . {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} In 1871, during {{ill|10=ja|11=津守國榮|Kunimi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} 's reign, he was elevated to the peerage as a member of a prestigious shrine family, and on July 8, 1884, he was elevated to the Rank of [[baron]] . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|小田部雄次|2006}} == Genealogy == {| class="wikitable" ! colspan="7" |Source{{Cite [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}} '''The Tsumori clan''' (津守氏) was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic [[:en:Shake (social class)|Shrine family]]. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} Shrine ( [[:en:Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Sumiyoshi Ward]], [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net|qq=draft|qq=draft}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato kingship|qq=}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayato people|qq=}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|qq=}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Amabe clan|Amabe]], and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, [[:en:Takakuraji|Takakuraji]], as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998th year ） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, [[:en:Gōzoku|a powerful]] lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the [[:en:Yodo River|Yodo River]], which is the entrance to [[:en:Nara Basin|the Yamato Plain]], flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of [[:en:Japanese missions to Tang China|the Tang Dynasty missions]] . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]], {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even Ranked as {{ill|10=ja|11=Kugyō|Kugyō|lt=nobles|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} . {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} In 1871, during {{ill|10=ja|11=津守國榮|Kunimi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} 's reign, he was elevated to the peerage as a member of a prestigious shrine family, and on July 8, 1884, he was [[津守国栄]]|後裔=[[笠嶋氏]]（[[社家]]）}} '''The Tsumori clan''' (津守氏) was a [[Japan|Japanese]] [[clan]] that was an aristocratic [[:en:Shake (social class)|Shrine family]]. The family has a lineage dating back to ancient times and is the hereditary chief priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} Shrine ( [[:en:Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Sumiyoshi Ward]], [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]] [[Osaka|City, Osaka Prefecture]] ). After [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], the family also became a [[Baron|baronial]] family of the nobility. {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} The Tsumori clan is a Japanese clan. They have run {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]].{{Cite web|title=Sumiyoshi Taisha|url=http://www.digital-images.net/Gallery/Scenic/Japan/Shrines/Sumiyoshi/sumiyoshi.html|access-date=2023-11-27|website=www.digital-images.net|qq=draft|qq=draft}} They are descended from the ''Tenson-zoku'' as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}''{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The Tsumori clan, whose members have succeeded the position of head priest of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} since the reign of [[Emperor Ōjin]], are the descendants of Tamomi no Sukune's son, Tsumori no Toyoada (or Tsumori no Toyonogodan). == Tenson zoku == {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato kingship|qq=}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It mentions that the [[Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]], the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|lt=Hayato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayato people|qq=}} descended from the Tenson tribe.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|user:immanuelle/reed bed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today. == Genealogy == The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tamba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|qq=}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tamba Province|lt=Tanba|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Amabe clan|Amabe]], and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, [[:en:Takakuraji|Takakuraji]], as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == history == The Tsumori clan is said to be a clan descended from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉大社神代記|Taisha Jindai-ki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]] and [[Emperor Keikō]], Ominagata no Mikoto’s son, Omitanosukune, was active at the shrine. 田中卓『住吉大社神代記の研究』田中卓著作集７（図書刊行会、1998th year ） It is said that the family descended from Tanino Sukune, [[:en:Gōzoku|a powerful]] lord in {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉郡|Sumiyoshi-gun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} [[Settsu Province]] . When Taminosukune welcomed [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]], who returned from {{ill|10=ja|11=三韓征伐|the expedition to Silla|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[200|200,]] at Shichido Beach (Shichido [[Sakai, Osaka|, Sakai City]] [[Osaka Prefecture|, Osaka Prefecture]] ) (then Sumiyoshi County ), he asked Taminosukune to {{Ruby-ja|祀|まつ}} the three Sumiyoshi gods, since [[Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu]] had the divine power of [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|the three Sumiyoshi]] gods. In addition, the area around the mouth of the [[:en:Yodo River|Yodo River]], which is the entrance to [[:en:Nara Basin|the Yamato Plain]], flourished as a key transportation hub from early on, and the Yamato Imperial Court gave them the duty of protecting the ports, from which the Tsumori clan name also derives. While serving the Sumiyoshi Shrine for generations, they also led the Umi clan and mastered navigation techniques. The first evidence that the clan was called Tsumori dates back to the time of {{ill|10=ja|11=津守宿禰国磨|Tsumori no Sukune Kunimasa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, who traveled to the sea as a member of [[:en:Japanese missions to Tang China|the Tang Dynasty missions]] . In the late Heian period, {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国基|Kunimoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was also well known as a poet and was active in areas other than his role as a priest. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} According to the Sumiyoshi Genealogy and the Genealogy of the Sumiyoshi Shrine Priests and Their Clan, Kunimoto is known as the founder of the Tsumori clan revival. {{Kotobank|津守氏|日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)、ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典、世界大百科事典 第２版}} During [[Nanboku-chō period|the Nanboku-cho period]], {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国夏|Kunika|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=津守国久|Kunihisa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} were active as military commanders of the Southern Court. {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} During the Edo period, some of them even Ranked as {{ill|10=ja|11=Kugyō|Kugyō|lt=nobles|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} . {{Sfn|森岡浩|2012}} In 1871, during {{ill|10=ja|11=津守國榮|Kunimi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} 's reign, he was elevated to the peerage as a member of a prestigious shrine family, and on July 8, 1884, he was elevated to the Rank of [[baron]] . {{Sfn|華族大鑑刊行会|1990}} {{Sfn|小田部雄次|2006}} == Genealogy == {| class="wikitable" ! colspan="7" |Source{{Cite
